## Gates

`just check` (the `check-hygiene` target) runs `ops-check`, `ops-docs check`,
`tasks check`, assembly validation and Python compilation; the pre-commit hook runs it.
`python3 bin/assemble-instructions check` compares the selected artifact and manifest
with the catalog and the live ops renderer. Relevant staged changes select the entire
index; otherwise it checks disk. The executing assembler must equal its index bytes in
a staged check.

Use `just test-one tools/test_assemble_instructions.py -k staged` for staged cases.
`just test-one` runs serially. `just test-fast` and `just test` both cover all tests in
`tools/` on 4 pytest-xdist workers; there is no affected-only selection. Tests run in
the locked environment `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` declare: `just setup` installs it
into `.venv` on the system interpreter, and the test recipes refuse, naming
`just setup`, while it is missing. Rerun `just setup` after a system Python upgrade or
a lock change.

`.tt.toml` sets `automatic_broad = false`: locally, `just test` and `just test-fast`
record a skip instead of running. `just test-full` (`TT_FORCE=1 just test`) is the
deliberate local full run. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `just setup` and the full
suite with `TT_FORCE=1` on every branch push to `origin`. `just test-live` runs
`tools/test_claude_profile.py` against the live ops checkout the host registry names
under every policy. ops is private, so the hosted run sets `LORE_TEST_LIVE_OPS=unavailable`,
which makes the suite routes (`test`, `test-fast`) skip those 12 tests with a stated
reason; any other value fails collection, and `test-live` ignores the marker. Both
pre-push recipes run hygiene (timed as the hook), then `test-live`, then `test`
(full route) or `test-fast` (when every pushed ref is covered by CI, the fast route).
Since that split, hook timings cover hygiene only and are not comparable with earlier
ones. Historical proof commands are acceptance checks outside the recurring gates.

For a new obligation, use `python3 bin/assemble-instructions add-rule <fragment-id>
--start-line N --end-line M --title TEXT`. After editing existing rule prose, run
`python3 bin/assemble-instructions refresh`, resolve exact selectors, then
`just assemble`. Staged-source refusal means unstage named files keeping edits,
refresh, inspect and restage. `python3 bin/assemble-instructions provenance`
reports all claims and warnings; repeat `--context FILE` for target contexts.
See `docs/instruction-assembly.md` for interrupted-operation recovery and coverage
exclusions. Check validates selected rule/exclusion/schema files; unknown history
is a warning, while broken bindings or uncovered obligations are fatal.

## Layout

- `instructions/AGENTS.md`: generated global instructions served through hq
  `./links.toml`; `instructions/AGENTS.manifest.json`: generated provenance.
  Root `AGENTS.md` is this repository's guide.
- `instructions/assembly.toml` and `instructions/fragments/`: editable catalog and
  policy sources. Ops owns the external Projects fragment.
- `profiles/`: the personal, work and external fragments resolved by ops-profile.
- `skills/`: the `curate-docs` skill, `skills/references/` (lore-authored retention
  guidance and schemas) and the skill README.
- `vendor/superpowers` and `vendor/agent-skills`: the pinned submodules; `just setup`
  initializes them.
- `bin/skill-sizes.py`: the skill inventory utility.
- `docs/`: the reference documents (`instruction-formats.md`, `profile-delivery.md`,
  `instruction-assembly.md`). Specs, plans, briefs and the provenance audit live in the
  records root (`tasks where` names it). This repository's history no longer holds the
  19 documents archived there; the records repository keeps theirs in its lore directory
  (`git -C <records root> log --follow -- lore/docs/<path>`). Two history rewrites
  changed commit ids. A commit from before the 2026-11-05 rewrite, which removed vendored
  agent-skills copies, maps through the agent-skills-commit-map-v2.txt attachment on
  lore-1be62d (old and new id per line; zeros mark a pruned commit). A commit from before
  the 2026-10-27 rewrite first maps through the combined-map.json attachment on
  lore-72153d (to its rewritten commit, its records-archive commit, or both), then
  through the lore-1be62d map. `tasks show <task>` prints each attachment's path.
- `hooks/claude-profile`: the SessionStart hook every Claude Code and Codex session runs,
  wired from hq's hook files; it reaches ops's resolver through the tasks registry.
- `bin/assemble-instructions`: the sole artifact/manifest writer and guard.
  `tools/`: assembly tests, pinned proof driver and vendored tooling;
  task records live in the records root.

## Rules

- `hooks/claude-profile` never exits non-zero and never blocks a session; every failure is
  one `profile: unresolved` line. A change to it is verified by the text a fresh session
  shows, never by its exit status, which proves nothing.

- The linked global artifact and manifest are generated; do not edit either by
  hand. Edit `instructions/fragments/…`, then run `just assemble`.
- The manifest records `bin/assemble-instructions`' own blob id and sha256, so an
  edit to the assembler stales it even when the rendered instructions are unchanged.
  Run `just assemble` and stage the manifest in the same commit; only its assembler
  entry may change.
- Ops owns the Projects/Feedback-owners source. Edit identity declarations there,
  run just projects in ops, then `just assemble` here. Assembly is the only writer
  of delivered instructions and provenance; both checks must pass.
- Deployed gates always use registered owner roots. Preparation environment
  values cannot redirect them; explicit CLI source overrides announce their
  input and require the registered repository identity.
- Keep `vendor/superpowers` at the release Claude Code's installed plugin runs
  (`~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`). A bump that adds or removes a skill
  needs a commit here and a declaration in hq `./links.toml`, or harnesses run
  different skills.
- Keep `vendor/agent-skills` at an upstream release tag. A bump that changes the
  selected skills needs the hq declarations, on both surfaces, in the same change set.
